To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the amino acid sequence of Cμ4 of a salamander, A. mexicanum, is highly homologous to that of the same domain of the IgM of other vertebrates and that the sequence of this domain is useful to reconstruct a phylogenetic tree of vertebrates.
the axolot μ chain is similar to the X. laevis μ and that the Cμ4 domain is a useful phylogenetic marker for the study of the evolution of the vertebrates.

we have cloned the complete Cμ region of the axoltl IgM, and have shown that the four Cμ regions of 13 vertebrates are related by a continuous line of evolutionary descent, and can be used to reconstruct the phylogeny of vertebrates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the evolution of the vertebrates IgM.
the evolution of immunoglobulins and the genes encoding these proteins.
the molecular biology of the IgM molecule in the axolot, Ambystoma mexicann.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all vertebrate IgM chains have evolved from a single ancestral gene.
the evolution of the vertebrates has followed a continuous path, and that the IgM has been present in the common ancestor of all extant vertebrate species.

all the vertebrate μ chains, from the earliest to the latest, are the product of a single ancestral gene which has been evolving in a continuous line since the origin of vertebrates, about 500 million years ago.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Cμ4 domain is the most conservative part of the vertebrate Cμ and the one that is most likely to be involved in the binding of the μ chain to the membrane.
the Cμ domains have evolved at a rate which is slower than that of the V‐region domains, and that the Cμ4 domain has evolved faster than the others.
the evolution of the vertebrates has led to the conservation of the μ constant domain structure which was already present in the common ancestor of all living species.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the evolution of the Cμ domain is a continuous and progressive event, with a very strong conservation of the Cμ1 domain, a less conserved Cμ2 domain, a highly conserved Cμ3 domain, and a highly conserved secretory tail.
the evolution of the vertebrates IgM chain is a continuous process, and the IgM chain is not an ancestral Ig chain.
the evolution of the Cμ domains is not a simple process.
